issue.title: 3.1.2 regression: `stream_with_context` triggers `teardown_request()` calls before response generation
issue.author: noirbee

summary.text: The issue reports a Flask 3.1.2 regression where `stream_with_context()` causes `teardown_request()` to run before the streamed response body is generated, and then again at the end of the request, which can break code that assumes `g` is still available during generator execution. A maintainer confirmed it will be fixed as a side effect of #5812 in Flask 3.2 and noted the docs already warn that teardown callbacks should not assume a specific number or timing of invocations.

known_facts.text: The reporter’s minimal example sets `g.hello = "world"`, returns `stream_with_context(generate())`, and shows that in Flask 3.1.2 `do_teardown_request()` runs before the generator starts, then again after the request, causing `g.pop("hello")` to fail with `KeyError`/`AttributeError`-related output.
In Flask 3.1.1, the reporter observed `Starting to generate response` before the teardown callback, with only one teardown call after the request finished.
A maintainer said the problem will be fixed as a side effect of #5812 in Flask 3.2, and invited a PR if someone could solve it earlier without reintroducing the other issue.

The reporter replied that the key concern is the timing of teardown before entering the generator, not only repeated teardown calls, and they linked the behavior to the documented meaning of `do_teardown_request()` as being called after the request is dispatched and the response is returned.
Another user confirmed the same behavior on Flask 3.2.0.dev0, showing two teardown calls and the same streamed-response failure trace.
A later commenter asked whether the fix would land in 3.2.0, and a maintainer answered yes.

content.draft_reply:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This matches the regression we’ve seen in 3.1.2: `stream_with_context()` is triggering `teardown_request()` too early, and the extra teardown call at the end is also part of the same bad lifecycle change.

This should be corrected as part of #5812 in Flask 3.2. In the meantime, I don’t have a safe workaround to suggest beyond pinning to 3.1.1 if this is blocking you. Also, as the docs note, teardown callbacks should not rely on a specific number or exact timing of invocations, so any code there should be made idempotent.

If you still need a short-term workaround, could you confirm whether making the teardown callback idempotent is enough for your case, or whether the early call itself breaks the response generator logic?

I searched for related issues and read one candidate issue for comparison; no other candidate was read.
The repository label catalog is partial only in the sense that it lists the active labels available on this repo; no additional label was obviously justified beyond the evidence here.

comparisons.reason: Both issues involve `stream_with_context()` and context/teardown behavior during streamed responses, but the failure modes differ. This issue is about `teardown_request()` running before generator execution in Flask 3.1.2, while #6123 is about an abandoned generator leaving the app context stuck on a worker thread and preventing later `teardown_appcontext` calls. The shared area is streaming context lifecycle; the concrete bug and affected teardown phase are different.
similarities: Both concern `stream_with_context()` and the lifecycle of Flask request/app contexts during streamed responses.
Both describe teardown-related surprising behavior that can break code using context-bound state.
Both involve streamed responses and the timing/cleanup of context exit paths.
differences: This issue reports an early `teardown_request()` call before the generator starts, plus a second teardown call after the stream ends.
#6123 reports a leaked app context after client disconnect/abandoned iteration, with later requests on the same worker thread skipping `teardown_appcontext`.
This issue is tied to Flask 3.1.2 regression behavior during normal streaming; #6123 centers on disconnect/GC/cross-thread finalization and a stuck context state.
#6123 was read only from title/body and describes a different teardown hook (`teardown_appcontext`) and different failure condition.

sources.title: 3.1.2 regression: `stream_with_context` triggers `teardown_request()` calls before response generation
sources.excerpt:
Hello, I believe the changes to `stream_with_context()` in https://github.com/pallets/flask/pull/5799/commits/9822a0351574790cb66c652fcc396ad7aa2b09d8 introduced a bug where the `teardown_request()` callables are invoked too early in the request/response lifecycle (and actually invoked twice, before generating the response and a second time after the end of the request). Take the following example: ```python # flask_teardown_stream_with_context.py from flask import Flask, g, stream_with_context def _teardown_request(_): print("do_teardown_request() called") g.pop("hello") app = Flask(__name__) app.teardown_request(_teardown_request) @app.get("/stream") def streamed_response(): g.hello = "world" def generate(): print("Starting to generate response") yield f"

Hello {g.hello} !

" return stream_with_context(generate()) app.run(debug=True) ``` In 3.1.1: ``` % /tmp/venv/bin/flask --version Python 3.13.7 Flask 3.1.1 Werkzeug 3.1.3 % /tmp/venv/bin/python flask_teardown_stream_with_context.py […] Starting to generate response 127.0.0.1 - - [01/Sep/2025 16:07:05] "GET /stream HTTP/1.1" 200 - do_teardown_request() called ``` In 3.1.2: ``` % /tmp/venv/bin/flask --version Python 3.13.7 Flask 3.1.2 Werkzeug 3.1.3 % /tmp/venv/bin/python flask_teardown_stream_with_context.py do_teardown_request() called Starting to generate response do_teardown_request() called Debugging middleware caught exception in streamed response at a point where response headers were already sent. Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/helpers.py", line 132, in generator yield from gen File "/tmp/flask_teardown_stream_with_context.py", line 21, in generate yield f"

Hello {g.hello} !

" ^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/ctx.py", line 56, in __getattr__ raise AttributeError(name) from None AttributeError: hello During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/werkzeug/wsgi.py", line 256, in __next__ return self._next() ~~~~~~~~~~^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/werkzeug/wrappers/response.py", line 32, in _iter_encoded for item in iterable: ^^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/helpers.py", line 130, in generator with app_ctx, req_ctx: ^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/ctx.py", line 443, in __exit__ self.pop(exc_value) ~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/ctx.py", line 410, in pop self.app.do_teardown_request(exc) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/app.py", line 1356, in do_teardown_request self.ensure_sync(func)(exc) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ File "/tmp/flask_teardown_stream_with_context.py", line 7, in _teardown_request g.pop("hello") ~~~~~^^^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/flask/ctx.py", line 88, in pop return self.__dict__.pop(name) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^ KeyError: 'hello' 127.0.0.1 - - [01/Sep/2025 16:09:35] "GET /stream HTTP/1.1" 200 - ``` Specifically, ``` do_teardown_request() called Starting to generate response do_teardown_request() called ``` So `_teardown_request()` is called before flask start to iterate on the response generator. This is a simplified version of our own code; I'm not sure we can actually expect `g` to still be available during response generators, but given it worked in 3.1.1 and the phrasing / intent of `teardown_request()`, I'd expect it not to be called before the response is actually generated. Note also that removing the code which causes the error, i.e. the `g` access, and keeping just the `print()` for debugging, will still show `_teardown_request()` being called twice. It's not obvious to me where exactly the bug is triggered. Adding a `traceback.print_stack()` call to `_teardown_request()`: * in 3.1.1, the only call, once the request is done, is triggered by https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/7fff56f5172c48b6f3aedf17ee14ef5c2533dfd1/src/flask/helpers.py#L115 ⇒ https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/330123258e8c3dc391cbe55ab1ed94891ca83af3/src/flask/ctx.py#L443 * in 3.1.2, the (new) first call before entering the response generator is triggered by https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/330123258e8c3dc391cbe55ab1ed94891ca83af3/src/flask/app.py#L1527 ; the second is similar to 3.1.1, i.e. https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/330123258e8c3dc391cbe55ab1ed94891ca83af3/src/flask/helpers.py#L130 ⇒ https://github.com/pallets/flask/blob/330123258e8c3dc391cbe55ab1ed94891ca83af3/src/flask/ctx.py#L443 Environment: - Python version: 3.13 - Flask version: 3.1.2

sources.title: `stream_with_context`: abandoned generator leaves the app context current on the worker thread; later requests skip `teardown_appcontext`
sources.excerpt:
Title: `stream_with_context`: abandoned generator leaves the app context current on the worker thread; later requests skip `teardown_appcontext`
State: closed

`stream_with_context` pushes the request's contexts onto whichever thread iterates the response body, and pops them only if the generator completes or is closed on that same thread. When a client disconnects mid-stream, the server abandons the body iterator and GC finalizes it later — often on a different thread. That cross-context pop fails (`LookupError`/`ValueError` from `ContextVar.reset`, swallowed as "Exception ignored in ..."), and the app context stays current on the worker thread.

Because `RequestContext.push` reuses an ambient app context of the same app, every later request on that pooled thread runs under the stuck context and `teardown_appcontext` never fires for it. Anything keyed to the app context then leaks once per thread for the life of the process — with Flask-SQLAlchemy that is one connection held idle-in-transaction per poisoned thread, with nothing in the logs.

Related: #5774 fixed the same cross-context token failure for async views; #5804 covers teardown ordering in the 3.1.2 rewrite. Neither covers the abandonment case. The docs mention that headers/session need care with `stream_with_context`, but not that a disconnect can leave the context stuck on the thread — a warning there would be helpful even if the behavior itself is hard to change.

## Reproduction

One long-lived "worker" thread serves two requests; the abandoned body iterator is GC-finalized on the main thread in between (in real deployments the reference is dropped by server machinery outside the worker — servers may never call `close()` on the iterator after a disconnect):

```python
import gc
import queue
import threading

from flask import Flask, Response, stream_with_context
from flask.globals import _cv_app

app = Flask(__name__)
teardowns = []

@app.teardown_appcontext
def note_teardown(exc):
    teardowns.append(threading.current_thread().name)

@app.route("/stream")
def stream():
    def gen():
        for i in range(100):
            yield f"chunk{i}\n"
    return Response(stream_with_context(gen()))

@app.route("/plain")
def plain():
    return "ok"

abandoned = queue.Queue()   # holds the dropped iterator, like server machinery
step2 = threading.Event()

def worker():
    # --- request A: streaming response, client disconnects after one chunk ---
    with app.test_request_context("/stream"):
        rv = app.full_dispatch_request()
    body = iter(rv.response)
    next(body)   # first chunk: stream_with_context pushes app+request ctx HERE
    abandoned.put((body, rv))   # server-side reference outlives the request
    del body, rv
    print("A: ambient ctx after abandonment:", _cv_app.get(None))

    step2.wait()  # main thread GC-finalizes the generator meanwhile

    # --- request B: any later request on this pooled worker thread ---
    print("B: ambient ctx at request start:", _cv_app.get(None))
    teardowns.clear()
    with app.test_request_context("/plain"):    # reuses the ambient ctx of the
        app.full_dispatch_request()             # same app -> no fresh app ctx
    print("B: teardown_appcontext ran for B:", bool(teardowns))
    print("B: ambient ctx after B finished:", _cv_app.get(None))

t = threading.Thread(target=worker, name="wsgi-worker-0")
t.start()

abandoned.get()          # take the reference, then drop it on the MAIN thread
gc.collect()             # generator finalized here -> cross-context pop fails
step2.set()
t.join()
```

Output (Flask 3.1.3, Python 3.13):

```
Exception ignored in: <generator object stream_with_context.<locals>.generator at 0x...>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../flask/helpers.py", line 130, in generator
    with app_ctx, req_ctx:
  File ".../flask/ctx.py", line 284, in __exit__
    self.pop(exc_value)
  File ".../flask/ctx.py", line 264, in pop
    ctx = _cv_app.get()
LookupError: <ContextVar name='flask.app_ctx' at 0x...>
A: ambient ctx after abandonment: <flask.ctx.AppContext object at 0x10b49c830>
B: ambient ctx at request start: <flask.ctx.AppContext object at 0x10b49c830>
B: teardown_appcontext ran for B: False
B: ambient ctx after B finished: <flask.ctx.AppContext object at 0x10b49c830>
```

## Expected behavior

Request B runs under its own app context and `teardown_appcontext` fires when it finishes. Instead it silently runs under request A's leaked context, teardown never runs, and the thread stays poisoned indefinitely.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.13 (also reproduced on 3.11)
- Flask version: 3.1.3. The `main` branch (3.2-dev, post-#5639 merged context) looks affected as well: `stream_with_context` there enters the single context via `with ctx:` around the priming `yield None`, so the context is pushed at creation and only exited when the generator completes or is closed.

sources.title: Add support for RFC5861 Cache-Control headers
sources.excerpt:
[RFC5861](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5861) standardised two Cache-Control extensions:
1. `stale-while-revalidate`
2. `stale-if-error`

Please add support for these in the standard werkzerg `ResponseCacheControl`.

One use case of these extensions is to allow sites to have their CDNs "coalesce" requests for content when it goes stale.  Another is to serve a stale representation from the CDN when the site is having an outage.  It's possible to solve this problem without changes to werkzeug, but as it's a standard feature, I think it would be nice to have it in the library.
